curated_technique: Combination: number of ways to choose 2 items from 4 unordered, C(n,r)=n!/(r!(n-r)!).
Combination: choose 3 items from 7 unordered.
Combination: choose 1 item from 8.
Combination: choose 9 items from 10 (equivalently, leave 1 out).
Combination: choose 3 items from 5 unordered.
Permutation: arrange 2 items chosen in order from 3, P(n,r)=n!/(n-r)!.
Permutation: arrange 4 items chosen in order from 6.
Permutation: arrange 1 item chosen from 7 (equivalently, just 7).
Permutation: arrange 9 items chosen in order from 10.
Combination: choose 11 items from 12 (equivalently, leave 1 out).
Multiply independent choice counts (product rule): choose 1 from one group and 2 from another.
Product rule for two independent unordered selections.
Sum rule for two mutually exclusive selection cases.
Combine the product rule (for one case) and the sum rule (across cases).
Number of ways to choose a 4-student delegation from a class of 10, unordered.
Number of ways to pick 7 balls together (unordered) from a box of 10.
Number of ways to pick 4 balls in order from a box of 7 (ordered draw).
Circular-adjacent-to-linear arrangement count: (n-1)! ways to seat n people around a round table, expressed here as P(n-1,n-1).
Sum rule: choose 3 representatives that are all boys, or all girls, from 5 boys and 3 girls.
Product rule: choose 2 boys and 1 girl independently.
Complement counting ('at most 2 girls'): total ways minus the all-girls case.
Choose 4 teachers, all male, from a group of 5 male teachers.
Choose 4 teachers, all female, from a group of 4 female teachers.
Product rule: choose 2 male and 1 female teacher independently.
Product rule: choose exactly 1 male teacher and fill the rest with female teachers.
Sum rule: draw 3 red tickets, or 3 yellow tickets, from an envelope of 3 red + 4 yellow.
Product rule: choose 2 red and 1 yellow ticket independently.
Product rule: exactly 1 red ticket, remaining tickets yellow.
Complement counting ('no red ticket'... i.e. 'at least one red'): total minus the all-yellow case.
Number of ways to draw 3 flowers from a vase of 10 (6 white + 4 red), unordered.
Sum rule: choose 4 books all math, or all English, from 7 math + 5 English books.
Complement counting ('at least 1 physics book'): total ways minus the all-math case, from 7 math + 5 physics books choosing 4.
Product rule: choose 3 black pieces and 1 white piece independently.
Complement counting ('at least 1 black piece'): total ways minus the all-white case.
Ordered selection of 3 distinct digits from 9, forming a 3-digit number.
Multiples-of-5 count: fix the last digit as 5, then arrange the remaining 2 digits from the other 8 in order.
Sum rule: choose 4 papers all math, or all English.
Product rule: exactly 1 English paper, remaining papers math.
Sum rule over two mutually exclusive 'all one color' cases when drawing 4 balls from a box of 4 red + 6 black balls.
Sum rule across three mutually exclusive 'all same color' cases (yellow, white, red) when drawing 3 balls from a mixed box; a group too small to supply 3 contributes C(n,3)=0.
Number of ways to draw 2 spades together (unordered) from the 13 spades in a standard deck.
Product rule: one card from the 13 spades, one card from the 26 red cards.
